title: Fourth-moment decomposition under the noise operator
statement:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function, and let $\rho\in\bbr$. Write $g$ for
the average of $f$ over its last coordinate and $h$ for the corresponding
half-difference, so that
\[
  g(x)=\tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0)+f(x,1)\bigr),\qquad
  h(x)=\tfrac12\bigl(f(x,0)-f(x,1)\bigr)
\]
are Boolean functions of the first $n$ variables. Then the fourth moment of $T_\rho f$
under the uniform measure decomposes as
\[
  \E\bigl[(T_\rho f)^4\bigr]
  = \E\bigl[(T_\rho g)^4\bigr]
  + 6\rho^2\,\E\bigl[(T_\rho g)^2\,(T_\rho h)^2\bigr]
  + \rho^4\,\E\bigl[(T_\rho h)^4\bigr].
\] For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on n+1 variables
ρ is a real parameter (no constraint)
g is the average of f over its last coordinate
h is the half-difference of f over its last coordinate
replaced:
For $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$, writing $g = \mathrm{avgLast}\,f$ and
$h = \mathrm{diffLast}\,f$, the fourth moment of $T_\rho f$ decomposes as
\[
  \E[(T_\rho f)^4]
  = \E[(T_\rho g)^4] + 6\rho^2\,\E[(T_\rho g)^2 (T_\rho h)^2] + \rho^4\,\E[(T_\rho h)^4].
\]
